properties.title: Opinion: Microsoft is really in charge

edges.description: Microsoft has invested roughly $13 billion in OpenAI since 2019.
Microsoft holds a stake of about 27% in OpenAI Group PBC.
The nonprofit retains control of the company and appoints its board.
Nadella is chief executive of Microsoft.
Described as chief executive of OpenAI.
OpenAI depends on Azure cloud for most of its computing power.
Critics argue Microsoft has effective control over OpenAI's strategy; this is an opinion, not a stated fact.
Azure revenue is reported within Microsoft's quarterly results.

evidence.excerpt: The OpenAI Foundation, a nonprofit, retains control of the company and appoints its board.
evidence.reasoning: States that a party other than Microsoft retains control of OpenAI, which bears directly on whether Microsoft controls OpenAI.

evidence.excerpt: Microsoft holds a stake of about 27% in OpenAI Group PBC.
evidence.reasoning: Gives Microsoft's ownership stake in OpenAI, relevant to assessing whether Microsoft has control.

evidence.excerpt: Microsoft, OpenAI's largest outside investor, does not have a board seat and does not control OpenAI.
evidence.reasoning: Directly addresses the claim by stating Microsoft does not control OpenAI.

evidence.excerpt: The OpenAI Foundation holds the power to appoint all members of the board of directors of OpenAI Group PBC.
evidence.reasoning: Identifies who holds board appointment power, relevant to where control lies.

evidence.excerpt: Critics argue that Microsoft has effective control over OpenAI's strategy because of this dependence.
evidence.reasoning: States the claim of control, but attributes it to critics as opinion.

evidence.excerpt: Microsoft has exclusive rights to sell OpenAI models through Azure until 2032.
evidence.reasoning: Describes a contractual commercial right that bears on the degree of Microsoft's influence over OpenAI.

evidence.excerpt: Microsoft reported quarterly revenue of $77.7 billion.
evidence.reasoning: Reports Microsoft's revenue, but says nothing about OpenAI or control over it.

assessments.explanation: 1 independent source(s) support and 2 contradict the claim (weighted 0.40 vs 1.60).

sources.title: Microsoft and OpenAI rework partnership
sources.content: Microsoft has invested roughly $13 billion in OpenAI since 2019. Under the restructured agreement, Microsoft holds a stake of about 27% in OpenAI Group PBC. The OpenAI Foundation, a nonprofit, retains control of the company and appoints its board. Satya Nadella, chief executive of Microsoft, said the partnership remains strong.

sources.title: OpenAI Group PBC: governance summary
sources.content: OpenAI Group PBC is a public benefit corporation. The OpenAI Foundation holds the power to appoint all members of the board of directors of OpenAI Group PBC. Microsoft, OpenAI's largest outside investor, does not have a board seat and does not control OpenAI. Sam Altman is chief executive of OpenAI.

sources.title: Opinion: Microsoft is really in charge
sources.content: OpenAI depends on Microsoft's Azure cloud for most of its computing power. Critics argue that Microsoft has effective control over OpenAI's strategy because of this dependence. Microsoft has exclusive rights to sell OpenAI models through Azure until 2032.

sources.title: Azure growth beats estimates
sources.content: Microsoft reported quarterly revenue of $77.7 billion. Azure revenue grew 40%, led by AI services.
